newsitem.title: SPAIN: France Telecom mulls bid for Retevision.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom mulls bid for Retevision.

text.p: France Telecom is considering bidding with Deutsche Telekom for a 20 to 35 percent stake in the sale of Spanish broadcaster Retevision, the head of France Telecom in Spain told daily El Mundo.
In an interview published on Sunday, Patrick Teixido said the French telecommmunications group was, however, awaiting the details of the sale.
"We have already starting talking with (our Spanish partners)," Teixido told El Mundo. "The stake could be around 20 percent, 30 percent or even 35 percent."
"We will fall in line with the terms and timetable of Retevision's privatisation. But we are still awaiting the most important parameters of the sale," he added.

Retevision, Spain's second telecommunications operator after Telefonica de Espana, is due to be fully privatised by 2000. Spain intends to sell intitally between 51 and 60 percent of its share capiital.

Teixido said specification of connection charges would be an important factor in the sale. "There could be two competitors or 150...but if the charges are too high there will be no competition," he added.
France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom form part of the multinational consortium Global One together with America's Sprint.
Others tipped to be interested in competiting in the sale include British Telecommunications, Cable & Wireless, and a consortium formed by Spain's Endesa, Banco Central Hispano and Banco Santander.
